questions.q: The acute angle between the curves $x^2+y^2=x+y$ and $x^2+y^2=2 y$ is
questions.solution:
$x^2+y^2=x+y\qquad ....\mathrm{(i)}x^2+y^2=2 y\qquad ....\mathrm{(ii)}$
Add (i) and (ii),
$2 x^2+2 y^2-3 y-x=0\qquad ....\mathrm{(iii)}$
Subtract (i) from (ii),
$x+y=0\qquad ....\mathrm{(iv)}$
Differentiate (i) w.r.t. $x \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{2 x-1}{1-2 y}=m_1$
Differentiate (ii) w.r.t. $x \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{x}{y}=$
Angle between (i) and (ii) is given by
$\begin{aligned}
& \tan \theta=\left|\frac{m_1-m_2}{1+m_1 m_2}\right|=\left|\frac{\frac{2 x-1}{1-2 y}-\frac{x}{1-y}}{1+\frac{(2 x-1) x}{(1-2 y)(1-y)}}\right| \\
& \tan \theta=\left|\frac{(2 x-1)(1-y)-x(1-2 y)}{(1-2 y)(1-y)+(2 x-1) x}\right| \\
& =\left|\frac{x+y-1}{2 x^2+2 y^2-3 y-x+1}\right|
\end{aligned}$
Using (iii) and (iv)
$\tan \theta=|-1| \Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{4}$

\end{aligned}$

Given that $|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|=|\vec{c}|=\sqrt{3}$ and
$\begin{aligned} & (\vec{a}+\vec{b}-\vec{c})^2+(\vec{b}+\vec{c}-\vec{a})^2+(\vec{c}+\vec{a}-\vec{b})^2=36 \\ & \Rightarrow|\vec{a}|^2+|\vec{b}|^2+|\vec{c}|^2+2 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}-2 \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}-2 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}+|\vec{b}|^2 \\ & +|\vec{c}|^2+|\vec{a}|^2+2 \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}-2 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}-2 \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}+|\vec{c}|^2+|\vec{a}|^2 \\ & +|\vec{b}|^2+2 \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}-2 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}-2 \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}=36 \\ & \Rightarrow 3|\vec{a}|^2+3|\vec{b}|^2+3|\vec{c}|^2-2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a})=36 \\ & \Rightarrow 3[3+3+3]-2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a})=36 \\ & \Rightarrow 27-2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a})=36\end{aligned}\Rightarrow 2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a})=-9\qquad ...\mathrm{(i)}$

questions.q: An object is placed at a distance of 18 cm in front of a mirror. If the image is formed at a distance of 4 cm on the other side, then focal length, nature of the mirror and nature of image are respectively
options: 3.14 cm , concave mirror and real image
3.14 cm , convex mirror and real image
5.14 cm , convex mirror and virtual image
5.14 cm , concave mirror and virtual image
questions.solution:
For a spherical mirror, $\mathrm{u}=-18 \mathrm{~cm}, \mathrm{v}=4 \mathrm{~cm}\therefore$ By mirror formula, $\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{-18} \Rightarrow f=\frac{36}{7} \mathrm{~cm}=5.14 \mathrm{~cm}$
Also, $\mathrm{f}=+\mathrm{ve}$. So, mirror is convex and virtual image is formed.

questions.solution:

questions.q: The voltage gain and current gain of a transistor amplifier in common emitter configuration are respectively 150 and 50 . If the resistance in the base circuit is $850 \Omega$, then the resistance in the collector circuit is
questions.solution:
For CE configuration of transistor,
$\begin{aligned}
& A_v=150, \beta=50, R_B=850 \Omega \\
& \therefore \quad \text { Voltage gain, } A_v=\beta\left(\frac{R_0}{R_I}\right)=\beta\left(\frac{R_C}{R_B}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow 150=50 \times \frac{R_c}{850} \\
& \therefore R_c=3 \times 850=2550 \Omega
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A certain volume of a gas at 300 K expands adiabatically until its volume is doubled. The resultant fall in temperature of the gas is nearly (The ratio of the specific heats of the gas $=1.5$ )
questions.solution:
For adiabatic process,
$\begin{aligned}
& V_2=2 V_1, \gamma=1.5, T_1=300 \mathrm{~K} \\
& \therefore \quad \mathrm{TV}^{\gamma-1}=\text { constant } \Rightarrow \mathrm{T}_1 \mathrm{~V}_1^{\gamma-1}=\mathrm{T}_2 \mathrm{~V}_2^{\gamma-1} \\
& \Rightarrow 300\left(\mathrm{~V}_1\right)^{0.5}=\mathrm{T}_2\left(2 \mathrm{~V}_1\right)^{0.5} \\
& \therefore \quad \mathrm{~T}_2=300 \times\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{0.5}
\end{aligned}\therefore \quad$ Fall in temperature is
$\Delta \mathrm{T}=\mathrm{T}_1-\mathrm{T}_2=300\left(1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)=88 \mathrm{~K}$

questions.q: When 100 J of heat is supplied to a gas, the increase in the internal energy of the gas is 60 J . Then the gas is/can
questions.solution:
For a gas, $Q=100 \mathrm{~J}, \Delta \mathrm{U}=60 \mathrm{~J}\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \frac{\mathrm{Q}}{\Delta \mathrm{U}}=\frac{100}{60}=\frac{5}{3} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{nc}_{\mathrm{p}} \Delta \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{nc}_{\mathrm{v}} \Delta \mathrm{~T}}=\frac{5}{3} \Rightarrow \gamma=\frac{5}{3}=1.66
\end{aligned}\therefore \quad$ The gas is monoatomic.

questions.q: A pipe with 30 cm Length is open at both ends, which harmonic mode of the pipe resonates a 1.65 kHz source? (Velocity of sound in air $=330 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ )
questions.solution:
For open organ pipe,
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{l}=30 \mathrm{~cm}, \mathrm{f}=1.65 \mathrm{KHz} \\
& \therefore \mathrm{I}=\frac{\mathrm{n} \lambda}{2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=\frac{21}{\frac{\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{f}}}=\frac{2 \times 30 \times 10^{-2} \times 1.65 \times 10^3}{330} \\
& \therefore \mathrm{n}=3
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A small disc is on the top of a smooth hemisphere of radius ' R '. The smallest horizontal velocity ' $V$ ' that should be imparted to the disc so that disc leaves the hemisphere surface without sliding down is (there is no friction)
questions.solution:
At the top of hemisphere, $\mathrm{mg}-\mathrm{N}=\frac{\mathrm{mv}^2}{\mathrm{R}}$
For the disc leaves the hemisphere, $\mathrm{N}=0 \quad \therefore \mathrm{mg}=\frac{\mathrm{mv}^2}{\mathrm{R}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{v}=\sqrt{\mathrm{gR}}$
